editorial:
Imagine being a smart lawyer who is totally ignored just because you are a woman. That is exactly where Nicole finds herself. She gets so fed up with the sexist bosses in her small town that she steals money from her firm and runs away to Paris. To get a fresh start, she decides to dress and act like a man. It sounds like a bold plan for a new life, but things quickly go south. The movie has a heavy, sad feeling as you watch her try to fit in while her mental health falls apart. She gets mixed up in messy relationships and crime, and it feels more like a nightmare than a dream.

You will notice that the acting is strong, especially as Nicole loses her grip on reality. The pacing is a bit slow, and it is definitely a bummer of a story, but it keeps you curious about how far she will fall. If you like dark character studies, you should check this one out. Since it is an older film, you will want to find a high-quality version to see the detail in the costumes. Try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: By the end, Nicole completely loses touch with who she is. Her attempt to live as a man and her illegal activities catch up to her. The mental break becomes total, and she slips into full schizophrenia. There is no happy ending or big rescue. She ends up trapped in her own broken mind, showing that her attempt to escape her old life only led her to a much worse place.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gritty character studies and dark psychological dramas.
